title: Douglas Fir: Giant Douglas Firs You Can Visit
meta_description: The great timber tree of the Pacific Northwest. Seattle's Seward Park Big Tree still carries scars from fires in 1508 and 1701.
intro: Douglas fir grows wild down the Pacific coast of North America, and at home it is enormous and old. Seward Park's Big Tree in Seattle, put at 400 to 500 years, still carries the scars of fires in 1508 and 1701. Sylvia, across Lake Washington, is about eight metres round; a windstorm took her top off in 1993 and she has been growing a candelabra of new ones since. The Doerner Fir near Coos Bay is 84 metres tall, and Portland's Balch Creek fir 74. Everywhere else it is an import with a hard start date, since seed only left the Pacific Northwest for Europe in 1827, and it still outgrows the locals. Germany's tallest tree is Waldtraut vom Mühlwald, a Douglas fir planted near Freiburg in 1913 and measured at 67.85 metres in 2024. Hobart's went into the botanical gardens in 1894.
